claim: Schistosomiasis is second only to malaria as the most socioeconomically devastating parasitic disease.
source: Schistosomiasis, a disease caused by parasitic trematodes of the genus Schistosoma, is second only to malaria as the most socioeconomically devastating parasitic disease, with an estimated 252 million people infected worldwide in 2015 (Disease et al., 2016; Mortality and GBD 2015 Mortality and Causes of Death Collaborators, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Disease et al., 2016 and Mortality and GBD 2015 Mortality and Causes of Death Collaborators, 2016

claim: An estimated 252 million people were infected with schistosomiasis worldwide in 2015.
source: Schistosomiasis, a disease caused by parasitic trematodes of the genus Schistosoma, is second only to malaria as the most socioeconomically devastating parasitic disease, with an estimated 252 million people infected worldwide in 2015 (Disease et al., 2016; Mortality and GBD 2015 Mortality and Causes of Death Collaborators, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Disease et al., 2016 and Mortality and GBD 2015 Mortality and Causes of Death Collaborators, 2016

claim: Larval digenean trematodes use snails (gastropod mollusks) as intermediate hosts for transmission to a vertebrate host.
source: Larval digenean trematodes share a common feature in the use of snails (gastropod mollusks) as intermediate hosts for transmission to a vertebrate host (Esch et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Esch et al., 2002

claim: The snail Biomphalaria glabrata transmits Schistosoma mansoni, the predominant causal species of intestinal schistosomiasis.
source: The snail Biomphalaria glabrata transmits several species of trematode, including Schistosoma mansoni, the predominant causal species of intestinal schistosomiasis (Pila et al., 2016a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pila et al., 2016a

claim: Various genetically determined resistance phenotypes exist with respect to S. mansoni infection in B. glabrata.
source: Various genetically determined resistance phenotypes exist with respect to S. mansoni infection in B. glabrata (Richards, 1975a; Richards, 1975b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Richards, 1975a and Richards, 1975b

claim: BS-90 strain B. glabrata snails naturally resist S. mansoni infection.
source: Some B. glabrata snails (such as BS-90 strain) naturally resist S. mansoni infection.
evidence: Stated directly in the text based on established knowledge

claim: Susceptible B. glabrata (such as M-line strain) can develop transient levels of acquired resistance following previous exposure to incompatible or radiation-attenuated parasites.
source: Susceptible B. glabrata (such as M-line strain) can develop transient levels of acquired resistance following previous exposure to incompatible or radiation-attenuated parasites with modest cross protection to related digenean species (Lie and Heyneman, 1975; Lie et al., 1975; Sullivan et al., 1982).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lie and Heyneman, 1975; Lie et al., 1975; Sullivan et al., 1982

claim: The killing of S. mansoni larvae is associated with a haemocyte-mediated cytotoxic mechanism.
source: Using in vivo and in vitro models of B. glabrata snails, it has been demonstrated that the killing of S. mansoni larvae is associated with a haemocyte-mediated cytotoxic mechanism, and passive transfer of natural resistance to S. mansoni has been successfully accomplished when haemocytes from a susceptible B. glabrata strain are incubated in cell-free haemolymph (plasma) from a resistant strain (Bayne et al., 1980a; Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Loker and Bayne, 1982).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bayne et al., 1980a; Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Loker and Bayne, 1982

claim: Passive transfer of natural resistance to S. mansoni has been successfully accomplished when haemocytes from a susceptible B. glabrata strain are incubated in cell-free haemolymph (plasma) from a resistant strain.
source: Using in vivo and in vitro models of B. glabrata snails, it has been demonstrated that the killing of S. mansoni larvae is associated with a haemocyte-mediated cytotoxic mechanism, and passive transfer of natural resistance to S. mansoni has been successfully accomplished when haemocytes from a susceptible B. glabrata strain are incubated in cell-free haemolymph (plasma) from a resistant strain (Bayne et al., 1980a; Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Loker and Bayne, 1982).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bayne et al., 1980a; Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Loker and Bayne, 1982

claim: Haemocytes from resistant or susceptible B. glabrata strains do not appear to differ a priori in their cytotoxic capabilities.
source: Thus, haemocytes from resistant or susceptible B. glabrata strains do not appear to differ a priori in their cytotoxic capabilities, but their response requires activation by some humoral factor(s) (Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Vasquez and Sullivan, 2001), for proper recognition of S. mansoni and enhancing haemocyte cytotoxicity (Hahn et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Vasquez and Sullivan, 2001; Hahn et al., 2001

claim: Haemocyte response requires activation by some humoral factor(s) for proper recognition of S. mansoni and enhancing haemocyte cytotoxicity.
source: Thus, haemocytes from resistant or susceptible B. glabrata strains do not appear to differ a priori in their cytotoxic capabilities, but their response requires activation by some humoral factor(s) (Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Vasquez and Sullivan, 2001), for proper recognition of S. mansoni and enhancing haemocyte cytotoxicity (Hahn et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bayne et al., 1980b; Granath and Yoshino, 1984; Vasquez and Sullivan, 2001; Hahn et al., 2001

claim: BgFREPs are a large family of soluble lectins identified in B. glabrata.
source: Identified in B. glabrata, a large family of soluble lectins termed fibrinogen-related proteins (BgFREPs) attracted widespread interest because of their unique structure (Adema et al., 1997; Gordy et al., 2015), capacity for somatic diversification (Zhang et al., 2004), and immune function (Hanington et al., 2010; Hanington and Zhang, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Adema et al., 1997; Gordy et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2004; Hanington et al., 2010; Hanington and Zhang, 2011

claim: BgFREPs are composed of a C-terminal fibrinogen (FBG) domain and either one or two N-terminal immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) domains linked to the FBG domain by an interceding region (ICR).
source: BgFREPs are composed of a C-terminal fibrinogen (FBG) domain and either one or two N-terminal immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) domains linked to the FBG domain by an interceding region (ICR) (Léonard et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to Léonard et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2001

claim: BgFREP3 plays a central role in B. glabrata resistance to digenetic trematodes.
source: Numerous studies have implicated BgFREP3 as playing a central role in B. glabrata resistance to digenetic trematodes (Hanington et al., 2010; Hanington et al., 2012; Hanington and Zhang, 2011; Lockyer et al., 2012; Lockyer et al., 2008; Pila et al., 2017b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hanington et al., 2010; Hanington et al., 2012; Hanington and Zhang, 2011; Lockyer et al., 2012; Lockyer et al., 2008; Pila et al., 2017b

claim: BgFREP3 contains two tandem IgSF domains whereas BgFREP2 has one.
source: BgFREP3 contains two tandem IgSF domains whereas BgFREP2 has one (Léonard et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Léonard et al., 2001

claim: The expression of BgFREP2 in BS-90 snails is dramatically up-regulated (57-fold) after exposure to S. mansoni.
source: The expression of BgFREP2 in BS-90 snails is dramatically up-regulated (57-fold) after exposure to S. mansoni, whereas M-line snails do not feature such a drastic upregulation, thereby suggesting a role for BgFREP2 in resistance (Hertel et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hertel et al., 2005

claim: M-line snails do not feature a drastic upregulation of BgFREP2 after exposure to S. mansoni.
source: The expression of BgFREP2 in BS-90 snails is dramatically up-regulated (57-fold) after exposure to S. mansoni, whereas M-line snails do not feature such a drastic upregulation, thereby suggesting a role for BgFREP2 in resistance (Hertel et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hertel et al., 2005

claim: The time course for heightened BgFREP2 expression overlaps the interval within which sporocysts are encapsulated and killed.
source: Interestingly, the time course for heightened BgFREP2 expression overlaps the interval within which sporocysts are encapsulated and killed, and only occurs in BS-90 haemocytes (Dinguirard et al., 2018; Hertel et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dinguirard et al., 2018; Hertel et al., 2005

claim: Heightened BgFREP2 expression only occurs in BS-90 haemocytes.
source: Interestingly, the time course for heightened BgFREP2 expression overlaps the interval within which sporocysts are encapsulated and killed, and only occurs in BS-90 haemocytes (Dinguirard et al., 2018; Hertel et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dinguirard et al., 2018; Hertel et al., 2005

claim: BgFREP2 is reactive with S. mansoni polymorphic mucins (SmPoMucs) found on the tegumental surface of larval S. mansoni.
source: Furthermore it was reported that BgFREP2 is reactive with S. mansoni polymorphic mucins (SmPoMucs) found on the tegumental surface of larval S. mansoni (Moné et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Moné et al., 2010

claim: TEPs are key components of invertebrate and vertebrate immune responses, aiding in melanization, opsonization, and killing of invading pathogens.
source: TEPs are key components of invertebrate and vertebrate immune responses, aiding in melanization, opsonization, and killing of invading pathogens (Baxter et al., 2007; Blandin et al., 2008; Levashina et al., 2001; Pila et al., 2017a; Portet et al., 2018; Povelones et al., 2013; Yassine and Osta, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Baxter et al., 2007; Blandin et al., 2008; Levashina et al., 2001; Pila et al., 2017a; Portet et al., 2018; Povelones et al., 2013; Yassine and Osta, 2010

claim: BgTEP was first characterized as an alpha macroglobulin proteinase inhibitor.
source: BgTEP was first characterized as an alpha macroglobulin proteinase inhibitor, and has recently re-emerged as a molecule of interest due to its association with BgFREP2 and SmPoMucs, and the capacity to bind to various invading pathogens (Bender et al., 1992; Moné et al., 2010; Portet et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bender et al., 1992; Moné et al., 2010; Portet et al., 2018

claim: BgTEP has the capacity to bind to various invading pathogens.
source: BgTEP was first characterized as an alpha macroglobulin proteinase inhibitor, and has recently re-emerged as a molecule of interest due to its association with BgFREP2 and SmPoMucs, and the capacity to bind to various invading pathogens (Bender et al., 1992; Moné et al., 2010; Portet et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bender et al., 1992; Moné et al., 2010; Portet et al., 2018

claim: Biomphalysin is a cytolytic protein in B. glabrata belonging to the β pore-forming toxin (β-PFT) superfamily.
source: Biomphalysin is a cytolytic protein in B. glabrata belonging to the β pore-forming toxin (β-PFT) superfamily (Galinier et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Galinier et al., 2013

claim: Biomphalysin binds to the surface of S. mansoni sporocysts in the absence of plasma.
source: Biomphalysin binds to the surface of S. mansoni sporocysts in the absence of plasma, while its cytolytic activity is drastically increased when plasma is present, suggesting that other factor(s) within the plasma may mediate the conversion of the oligomeric pre-pore to a functional pore (Galinier et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Galinier et al., 2013

claim: Biomphalysin's cytolytic activity is drastically increased when plasma is present.
source: Biomphalysin binds to the surface of S. mansoni sporocysts in the absence of plasma, while its cytolytic activity is drastically increased when plasma is present, suggesting that other factor(s) within the plasma may mediate the conversion of the oligomeric pre-pore to a functional pore (Galinier et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Galinier et al., 2013

claim: The cell-free plasma of BS-90 snails contained more BgFREP3 than does M-line snail plasma.
source: We initiated our investigations with BgFREP3 because we observed that the cell-free plasma of BS-90 snails contained more BgFREP3 than does M-line snail plasma (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B

claim: BgTEP1 was identified in the eluent of rBgFREP3 pull-down experiments from both M-line and BS-90 strains.
source: Among the proteins identified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) in the eluent of these pull-down experiments was BgTEP1 (Figure 1C). We performed four replicate rBgFREP3 pull-down experiments, each yielded a band at approximately 200 kDa, which corresponded to the full-length BgTEP1, which was identified from both M-line and BS-90 strains (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1C

claim: A total of 17 unique peptides of BgTEP1 were obtained from the LC-MS/MS analysis.
source: From the LC-MS/MS analysis we obtained a total of 17 unique peptides, 16 peptides were detected from M-line strain, four peptides were from BS-90 strain, and three peptides were present in both BS-90 and M-line strains (Table. S2 and Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1D

claim: There was no significant difference in baseline BgTEP1 expression between M-line and BS-90 strains.
source: Background transcript abundance of BgTEP1 detected by qRT-PCR in M-line and BS-90 snails, suggested that there was no significant difference (p>0.05) in baseline BgTEP1 expression between the two strains (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The interaction of BgFREP3 with BgTEP1 doesn't require the involvement of any parasite components.
source: These results indicate that the interaction of BgFREP3 with BgTEP1 doesn't require the involvement of any parasite components.
evidence: Inferred from pull-down experiments showing interaction in the absence of parasites

claim: Biomphalysin was identified in both M-line and BS-90 plasma from rBgTEP1 pull-down experiments.
source: Biomphalysin (UniProtKB/TrEMBL: A0A182YTN9 and A0A182YTZ4) was identified in both M-line and BS-90 plasma from rBgTEP1 pull-down experiments and was also present in the pull-down studies using rBgFREP3 (Figure 1C and E).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1C and E

claim: Biomphalysin was also present in the pull-down studies using rBgFREP3.
source: Biomphalysin (UniProtKB/TrEMBL: A0A182YTN9 and A0A182YTZ4) was identified in both M-line and BS-90 plasma from rBgTEP1 pull-down experiments and was also present in the pull-down studies using rBgFREP3 (Figure 1C and E).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1C and E

claim: BgFREP2 was identified as one of two unique proteins in the BS-90 lane in rBgFREP3 pull-down experiments.
source: Comparing rBgFREP3 pull-down results between M-line and BS-90 B. glabrata identified two unique proteins in the BS-90 lane (Figure 1C). One of these proteins was BgFREP2 (UniProtKB/TrEMBL: A0A2C9L9F5) (Figure 1C and E, Figure 1—source data 4A).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1C

claim: BgFREP2 was identified from plasma of both M-line and BS-90 strains when rBgTEP1 was used as bait in pull-down experiments.
source: This contrasted with our other data in which BgFREP2 was identified from plasma of both M-line and BS-90 strains when rBgTEP1was used as bait in pull-down experiments (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1E

claim: A variant of BgFREP3 was identified as another unique protein in the BS-90 lane in the rBgFREP3 pull-down experiments.
source: Another unique protein identified from the BS-90 lane in the rBgFREP3 pull-down experiments was a variant of BgFREP3 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by LC-MS/MS data and Figure 1C

claim: BgFREP3, BgTEP1, Biomphalysin and BgFREP2 associate with each other in B. glabrata plasma.
source: These results suggest that BgFREP3, BgTEP1, Biomphalysin and BgFREP2 associate with each other in B. glabrata plasma, with M-line and BS-90 strains displaying differing interactomes.
evidence: Inferred from pull-down experimental results

claim: M-line and BS-90 strains display differing interactomes of immune factors.
source: These results suggest that BgFREP3, BgTEP1, Biomphalysin and BgFREP2 associate with each other in B. glabrata plasma, with M-line and BS-90 strains displaying differing interactomes.
evidence: Inferred from pull-down experimental results showing different protein interactions

claim: BgFREP3 specially interacts with BgFREP2 and another unique BgFREP3 variant only in BS-90 B. glabrata.
source: Our data indicates that BgFREP3 specially interacts with BgFREP2 and another unique BgFREP3 variant only in BS-90 B. glabrata.
evidence: Supported by pull-down experimental data

claim: rBgFREP3 interacts with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: Immunocytochemistry clearly showed that rBgFREP3 and combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were able to interact with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts (Figure 2), while rBgTEP1 and rBgFREP2 alone did not have such capabilities (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2

claim: The combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 interacts with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: Immunocytochemistry clearly showed that rBgFREP3 and combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were able to interact with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts (Figure 2), while rBgTEP1 and rBgFREP2 alone did not have such capabilities (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2

claim: rBgTEP1 alone does not interact with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: Immunocytochemistry clearly showed that rBgFREP3 and combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were able to interact with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts (Figure 2), while rBgTEP1 and rBgFREP2 alone did not have such capabilities (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2

claim: rBgFREP2 alone does not interact with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: Immunocytochemistry clearly showed that rBgFREP3 and combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were able to interact with the outer tegument of S. mansoni sporocysts (Figure 2), while rBgTEP1 and rBgFREP2 alone did not have such capabilities (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2

claim: Pre-combined rBgFREP2 and rBgTEP1 associate with S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: However, incubation of sporocysts with pre-combined rBgFREP2 and rBgTEP1 yielded a signal, suggesting that these two factors required complex formation prior to being able to associate with S. mansoni sporocysts (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 2

claim: BgFREP3 does not require BgTEP1 in order to associate with targets on the S. mansoni sporocyst surface.
source: These results indicate the mechanisms by which BgFREP3 and BgFREP2 recognize S. mansoni sporocysts are different, that is, BgFREP3 does not require BgTEP1 in order to associate with targets on the S. mansoni sporocyst surface while BgFREP2 relies on BgTEP1 to bind to S. mansoni sporocysts.
evidence: Inferred from immunocytochemistry experiments

claim: BgFREP2 relies on BgTEP1 to bind to S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: These results indicate the mechanisms by which BgFREP3 and BgFREP2 recognize S. mansoni sporocysts are different, that is, BgFREP3 does not require BgTEP1 in order to associate with targets on the S. mansoni sporocyst surface while BgFREP2 relies on BgTEP1 to bind to S. mansoni sporocysts.
evidence: Inferred from immunocytochemistry experiments

claim: rBgFREP3 forms a complex with rBgTEP1.
source: As expected, rBgFREP3 did form a complex with rBgTEP1 (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A

claim: The rBgFREP3-rBgTEP1 complex appears in a region of high molecular weight (>460 kDa).
source: The complex appeared in a region of high molecular weight (>460 kDa), and the signal decreased gradually with the decrease of rBgTEP1:rBgFREP3 ratios in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A

claim: rBgFREP3 exists as a high molecular weight multimer in a non-denatured state.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, rBgFREP3 was found as a high molecular weight multimer in a non-denatured state.
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A

claim: Far-Western blotting confirmed the interaction between rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1.
source: A band was detected in the lane with 2 μg of rBgTEP1, confirming the interaction between rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by far-Western blot data shown in Figure 3B

claim: BgFREP2 and BgTEP1 form immune complexes.
source: BgFREP2 and BgTEP1 have been shown to form immune complexes with SmPoMucs derived from S. mansoni (Moné et al., 2010), suggesting that BgFREP2 and BgTEP1 associate with each other in snail plasma.
evidence: Supported by citation to Moné et al., 2010 and inference

claim: Western blot under non-denaturing conditions showed a band (>460 kDa) after mixing rBgFREP2 and rBgTEP1.
source: The results of Western blot under non-denaturing conditions showed a band (>460 kDa) after mixing rBgFREP2 and rBgTEP1 (Figure 3C upper panel).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C

claim: rBgFREP2 does not exist as a multimer under non-denaturing conditions.
source: However, rBgFREP2 did not exist as a multimer under non-denaturing conditions (Figure 3C upper panel), which was consistent with the findings of (Zhang et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Zhang et al., 2008

claim: Far-Western blot verified the interaction between rBgFREP2 and rBgTEP1.
source: In addition, we further verified the interaction between rBgFREP2 and rBgTEP1 by Far-Western blot (Figure 3C lower panel).
evidence: Supported by far-Western blot data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Plasma from the resistant BS-90 strain of B. glabrata was able to kill 67% of S. mansoni sporocysts by 48 hr post incubation.
source: Plasma (haemoglobin-low/free) from the resistant BS-90 strain of B. glabrata snails was naturally able to kill 67% (SEM 3.7%; n = 10) of S. mansoni sporocysts by 48 hr post incubation, while plasma from the susceptible M-line strain, which killed 20% (SEM 4.5%; n = 10), was not significantly more effective than the medium control in which 13% (SEM 2.1%; n = 10) were killed at 48 hr (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Plasma from the susceptible M-line strain killed 20% of S. mansoni sporocysts by 48 hr post incubation.
source: Plasma (haemoglobin-low/free) from the resistant BS-90 strain of B. glabrata snails was naturally able to kill 67% (SEM 3.7%; n = 10) of S. mansoni sporocysts by 48 hr post incubation, while plasma from the susceptible M-line strain, which killed 20% (SEM 4.5%; n = 10), was not significantly more effective than the medium control in which 13% (SEM 2.1%; n = 10) were killed at 48 hr (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4A

claim: The combined addition of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 significantly increased M-line-plasma-mediated killing of S. mansoni sporocysts to 56% by 48 hr post incubation.
source: However, the combined addition of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 significantly increased M-line-plasma-mediated killing of S. mansoni sporocysts by 48 hr post incubation (56% [SEM 4.8%; n = 10]) compared to the application of either recombinant protein alone.
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4A

claim: The combined addition of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 rendered the capacity of M-line plasma to kill S. mansoni sporocysts statistically insignificant from BS-90 plasma.
source: The combined addition of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 rendered the capacity of M-line plasma able to kill S. mansoni sporocysts statistically insignificant from BS-90 plasma (p>0.05) (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Recombinant proteins, in the absence of B. glabrata plasma, did not display any capacity to kill S. mansoni sporocysts.
source: Recombinant proteins, in the absence of B. glabrata plasma, did not display any capacity to kill S. mansoni sporocysts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by control experiment data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A

claim: Catalase did not affect the S. mansoni sporocyst killing capacity of BS-90 plasma.
source: Catalase did not affect the S. mansoni sporocyst killing capacity of BS-90 plasma nor did it influence M-line plasma incubated with rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that other factors besides ROS were activated by rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 to mediate sporocyst killing.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: Catalase did not influence M-line plasma incubated with rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1.
source: Catalase did not affect the S. mansoni sporocyst killing capacity of BS-90 plasma nor did it influence M-line plasma incubated with rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that other factors besides ROS were activated by rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 to mediate sporocyst killing.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: Haemocytes derived from BS-90 strain B. glabrata were innately capable of destroying S. mansoni sporocysts, killing 88% of sporocysts after 48 hr of incubation in vitro.
source: Haemocytes derived from BS-90 strain B. glabrata were innately capable of destroying S. mansoni sporocysts, killing 88% (SEM 3.6%; n = 10) of sporocysts after 48 hr of incubation in vitro (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4B

claim: The basal ability of M-line haemocytes to kill sporocysts (13%) was not significantly different from the medium-alone control (13%).
source: The basal ability of M-line haemocytes to kill sporocysts (13% [SEM 3%; n = 10]) was not significantly different from the medium-alone control (13% [SEM 2.1%; n = 10]), and was only slightly increased by adding rBgFREP3 (24% [SEM 3.4%; n = 10]) at 48 hr (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Addition of rBgTEP1 significantly increased sporocyst killing by M-line haemocytes to 40%.
source: Addition of rBgTEP1 did significantly increase sporocyst killing by M-line haemocytes to 40% (SEM 3.9%; n = 10) (Figure 4B), however, this killing response was significantly enhanced to 61% (SEM 5.5%; n = 10) when rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were incubated with M-line haemocytes together (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4B

claim: The killing response of M-line haemocytes was significantly enhanced to 61% when rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were incubated together.
source: Addition of rBgTEP1 did significantly increase sporocyst killing by M-line haemocytes to 40% (SEM 3.9%; n = 10) (Figure 4B), however, this killing response was significantly enhanced to 61% (SEM 5.5%; n = 10) when rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 were incubated with M-line haemocytes together (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4B

claim: The combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 did not convey a killing capacity to M-line snails that paralleled BS-90 haemocytes.
source: However, the combination of rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 did not convey a killing capacity to M-line snails that paralleled BS-90 haemocytes (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by sporocyst killing assay data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Incubation of rBgFREP2 in combination with rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 enabled M-line haemocytes to kill S. mansoni sporocysts (83%) to statistically indistinguishable levels as BS-90 haemocytes (88%).
source: Incubation of rBgFREP2 in combination with rBgFREP3 and rBgTEP1 enabled M-line haemocytes to kill S. mansoni sporocysts (83% [SEM 4.8%; n = 6]) to statistically indistinguishable (p>0.05) levels as BS-90 haemocytes (88% [SEM 4.7%; n = 6]) (Figure 4C).

claim: The oxidation of haemoglobin is toxic to S. mansoni sporocysts in long-term cultures.
